module_title: Emergency Provisions - Approvals, Grounds, and Immunities
introduction: At this level, we focus on the parliamentary approval timelines for emergencies, the historic changes made by the 44th Amendment to prevent misuse, and the legal immunities granted to the President and Governors.

core_concepts.title: Parliamentary Approval Timelines
core_concepts.description: National Emergency (352) must be approved by Parliament within 1 month. President's Rule (356) and Financial Emergency (360) must be approved within 2 months.

core_concepts.title: Armed Rebellion vs. Internal Disturbance
core_concepts.description: Originally, Article 352 included 'internal disturbance'. The 44th Amendment Act (1978) replaced this vague term with 'armed rebellion' to prevent the misuse of emergency powers (as happened in 1975).

core_concepts.title: Failure to Comply with Union Directions (Article 365)
core_concepts.description: If a state fails to comply with directions given by the Union, it shall be lawful for the President to hold that a situation has arisen where the state government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution (leading to Article 356).

core_concepts.title: Immunity of President & Governors (Article 361)
core_concepts.description: The President or Governor is not answerable to any court for the exercise of their official duties. No criminal proceedings whatsoever can be instituted against them during their term of office.

important_entities.name: 44th Amendment Act (1978)
important_entities.significance: Introduced by the Morarji Desai government, this amendment made it significantly harder to declare and sustain a National Emergency, adding safeguards like the requirement of a written recommendation from the Cabinet.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The President can declare a National Emergency ONLY after receiving a 'written recommendation' from the Cabinet, not just on the verbal advice of the Prime Minister.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: National is Urgent (1), Others can wait (2)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: 1 month limit for National Emergency (352); 2 months limit for State (356) and Financial (360).

exam_strategy_tips: Distinguish clearly between Article 356 and Article 365. Both lead to President's Rule, but 365 is specifically triggered by defying Central directions.
Note that President's Rule (356) can be extended for a maximum period of 3 years, whereas a National Emergency can be extended indefinitely (subject to 6-month approvals).
